title: Lights CPU Performance problems
body: ### Tested versions Reproduced in 4.5 Stable Reproduced in 4.5 Beta 7 Reproduced in 4.4 Stable Reproduced in 4.3 Stable Reproduced in 4.2 Stable? Reproduced in 4.1 Stable? Reproduced in 4.0 Stable? (4.2-4.0 report different, significantly lower values but the graph size looks the same, so probably misreported) ### System information Godot v4.5.beta7 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21013.1000) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10105F CPU @ 3.70GHz (8 threads) - 15.87 GiB memory ### Issue description After seeing some odd CPU performance issues in my Game I narrowed it down to the great many Lights being rendered, and I've made this MRP to test what's going on, and here's what the Visual Profiler Shows Highest usage is with Lights and Mesh Tiles active The dip is the next run With the Mesh Tiles replaced by a single plane The third plane is turning off the lights and turning on the mesh tiles in the next run Further notes from the Game, The rendering is clearly impacting the main thread even when trying to use separate thread for rendering, given the performance improves substantially when either less lights are rendered or less Game logic is being run Also Important note is that both Lights and Mesh Tiles are Moving! ### Steps to reproduce Open MRP, with the two Node3Ds visible (top one is lights, bottom one is individual mesh instance tiles) Observe extremely high CPU time in Preparing to Render 3D scene Hide the 2nd Node3D to hide the tiles and show the Mesh Instance below Hide the Mesh Instance and Reshow the 2nd Node3D but hide the 1st Node3D to hide the Lights ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [Lights.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22285601/Lights.zip)
